messages:
From: ops@quickcart.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in 95th/99th latency affecting checkout (US region)

Hi team,

We observed a sustained increase in 95th/99th p95/p99 latencies for /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints between 2027-04-11T02:12:00Z and 2027-04-11T02:46:00Z (US-west). The spike coincided with heavier checkout traffic; some users saw timeouts at the client (JS fetch errors, 504). Our telemetry shows tail latency jumps from ~180ms to ~1.8s at p99.

Can you confirm whether this window qualifies for an SLA review / credit eligibility? We need the verified outage/impact window and what evidence you will provide for our procurement team.

Attached: initial heartbeat summary from our side.

Thanks,
Sara Patel
Engineering Manager, QuickCart
ops@quickcart.com

Attachment: initial_heartbeat_summary.csv (CSV stub)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Sara Patel <sara@quickcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 95th/99th latency affecting checkout (US region)

Sara — thanks for the heads up and the summary. We're opening a ticket (INF-5921) and will pull the serving traces and request-level metadata. To speed validation, can you confirm:

- Which exact endpoints you consider user-facing for this claim (/v1/generate, /v1/chat, or both)?
- Sample request IDs or timestamps you saw client-side 504s for (if available).
- Whether you want the remedy (if eligible) as a pro-rata monthly credit or a one-time invoice credit.

I’ve looped in Ben (SRE) and Evelyn (Customer Success). We’ll get an initial impact assessment within 24 hours and an evidence bundle within 48 hours.

Next steps: we’ll run the SLO eligibility checks against the 99.9% availability target, produce the raw trace bundle, and share the preliminary calculation.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: sara@quickcart.com
Date: 2027-04-11T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 95th/99th latency affecting checkout (US region)

Quick summary of initial findings (preliminary, internal):

- Traces pulled for 2027-04-11T02:00:00Z–2027-04-11T03:00:00Z show a clear spike in tail latency aligned with a burst of cache evictions on the KV prefix used by the reproduction cache. Evictions started ~02:10Z and peaked ~02:25Z.
- Affected hosts: gw-usw2-03, gw-usw2-07. Kernel-level metrics show increased GC/compaction pauses on the quantized runtime on those workers.
- User-facing error rate (5xx/timeout) increased from baseline 0.02% to 0.9% during the window; most requests retried successfully but with higher latency.

SLO assessment (quick pass): our documented availability SLO is 99.9% measured on a per-route 5-minute rolling window. From the request logs, there were ~34 five-minute windows in the region that dipped below the 99.9% threshold; aggregating those windows gives ~11.5 minutes of impact where the route-level availability was below target.

What we will provide:
- Raw trace bundle (S3 link) with redaction as required.
- Per-route five-minute availability table and token-minute calculation used for pro-rata credit.
- A short RCA draft indicating safe root cause: cache pressure + runtime compaction interacting with eviction policy.

I recommend we propose a remedy of a pro-rata credit equal to the ratio of impacted minutes to the monthly window multiplied by the monthly service fee for the affected route(s). Evelyn / Rishi — confirm if QuickCart prefers a dollar credit or usage credit.

Attachment (internal): latency_histogram.png (summary chart)
From: Sara Patel <sara@quickcart.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T07:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 95th/99th latency affecting checkout (US region)

Thanks Ben — that aligns with what our traces show. We confirm the affected endpoints are /v1/checkout (proxying to /v1/generate) and /v1/chat. We’ve attached a prod trace with sample request IDs and a few client logs (prod-trace-5721.zip).

QuickCart preference: a one-time invoice credit is simpler for procurement. Could you include the exact formula you’ll use to compute the credit (so our finance team can accept it)? Also, please confirm the expected timeline for a postmortem and whether any mitigations will be deployed proactively to avoid recurrence.

—Sara
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Sara Patel <sara@quickcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-13T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 95th/99th latency affecting checkout (US region)

Sara — thanks for the trace bundle. Confirming next steps and what you’ll receive: 

1) Verified impact window: 2027-04-11T02:12:00Z — 2027-04-11T02:46:00Z (US-west routing).
2) Evidence bundle (to be shared within 48 hours): per-route five-minute availability table; raw trace archive (S3 link); host-level metrics and eviction logs.
3) Proposed remedy: one-time invoice credit computed as (impacted_minutes / total_minutes_in_billing_cycle) * monthly_charge_for_affected_routes.
   - Using the preliminary numbers Ben provided (11.5 impacted minutes), and QuickCart’s monthly billing window of 43,200 minutes, the pro-rata factor = 11.5/43200 ≈ 0.000266. If the monthly route charge is $12,000 (example), the credit would be ≈ $3.20. We’ll run the exact calculation against your billing record and send a formal credit memo.
4) Postmortem timeline: draft RCA within 5 business days; final postmortem and mitigation plan within 10 business days. Engineering will propose a mitigation (adjusted eviction policy + runtime compaction tuning) to be staged in canary next week.

If that approach sounds good, we’ll mark this as an SLA-eligible incident and move forward with the evidence pull and credit memo.

Best,
Rishi
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/INF-5921
